montirelin.text: Montirelin is a stable TRH analogue that appears in peptide and nootropic discussions as a wakefulness and neuroprotection compound, with some users linking alertness to staying consistent with training and routines. The appearance link is speculative; it has been studied in animals for arousal, with essentially no human trial data.

glypromate.text: Glypromate (GPE) is an IGF-1-derived tripeptide discussed in peptide circles for brain protection and recovery, which some users tie to better focus and consistency. It has no documented appearance use; the evidence is laboratory neuroprotection research, and its analogue trofinetide became an approved Rett syndrome drug.

trofinetide.text: Trofinetide is an approved prescription drug for Rett syndrome and a GPE analogue, so it comes up in peptide discussions as a relative of Glypromate. No appearance use is documented; it is used as a disease treatment and studied in that setting.

fosgonimeton.text: Fosgonimeton is an investigational Alzheimer's drug that acts as a prodrug of dihexa, a compound popular in nootropic circles. It was developed for dementia rather than any cosmetic purpose, and no appearance data exist; the evidence is limited to clinical research on cognition.

bnn-20.text: BNN-20 is a DHEA-derived "microneurotrophin" discussed in research-chemical circles for brain protection. It has no documented appearance use; the evidence is preclinical, mainly Parkinson's mouse models, with no human data.

bnn-27.text: BNN-27 is a DHEA-derived NGF mimetic described by its developers as lacking hormonal activity, and it is discussed in research-chemical circles for nerve and brain protection. No appearance use is documented; the evidence is preclinical with no human data.

n-acetyl-selank-amidate.text: This acetylated, amidated Selank analogue is sold as a research chemical, with users hoping for calmer mood and more social ease than the parent peptide. The appearance link is indirect and anecdotal; the analogue itself has no direct studies, and the evidence relates to Selank.

n-acetyl-semax-amidate.text: This acetylated, amidated Semax analogue is sold as a research chemical, with users seeking sharper focus and stamina than the parent peptide. Any appearance link runs through habit consistency and is anecdotal; the analogue itself has no direct studies, and the evidence relates to Semax.

dnsp-11.text: DNSP-11 is an experimental GDNF-derived peptide discussed in nootropic circles for dopamine neuron support. No appearance use is documented; it has been studied only in rats and monkeys, with no human trials.

fgl.text: FGL is a synthetic fragment of a neural adhesion protein discussed in nootropic circles for memory and brain plasticity. No appearance use is documented; the evidence is rodent memory data with no human trials.

chain: Nerve growth factor on the cornea
cenegermin.text: Cenegermin is a prescription nerve growth factor eye drop approved for neurotrophic keratitis, and it appears in peptide discussions as an NGF product. It has no documented appearance use; it is studied and approved for a rare corneal disease.

mecasermin-rinfabate.text: Mecasermin rinfabate is an IGF-1/IGFBP-3 injectable made for rare growth failure, and height-focused forum posters sometimes ask whether IGF-1 products could add height. That use is untested; it was studied only in children with growth disorders, and no data support height gain in people with normal growth.

axokine.text: Axokine is a CNTF-based injectable developed as an obesity drug to reduce body weight through a leptin-like mechanism. It was discontinued; trials showed small weight loss, with antibodies developing in most users, and it is mentioned mainly as a historical fat-loss compound.

kttks.text: KTTKS, sold as Matrixyl in palmitoylated form, is a collagen-signalling peptide used in anti-wrinkle skincare to smooth fine lines. It has a modest split-face trial, with open questions about how well it penetrates skin.

palmitoyl-tripeptide-38.text: Palmitoyl tripeptide-38 (Matrixyl Synthe'6) is a cosmetic signal peptide sold as a collagen booster to reduce wrinkles and firm skin. The evidence for that use is mostly supplier data and multi-ingredient serum studies.

glycyl-prolyl-hydroxyproline.text: Gly-Pro-Hyp is a collagen-derived tripeptide found in oral collagen supplements, which people take for skin firmness and wrinkles. It is absorbed in animals; human skin trials have used collagen hydrolysates, with none of the peptide itself.

ahk-cu.text: AHK-Cu is a copper tripeptide marketed in hair-care products and discussed in appearance circles as a hair-growth ingredient, much as GHK-Cu is for skin. The evidence for hair growth so far comes from cell-culture research.

ll-37.text: LL-37 is the body's own antimicrobial skin peptide, and forum posters discuss it for clearing acne, healing skin and anti-aging. These uses are based on its immune biology and anecdote, with no cosmetic trials behind them.

heberprot-p.text: Heberprot-P is a Cuban injectable EGF used for diabetic foot ulcers, and it comes up in discussions of EGF for skin healing and renewal. Wound-healing evidence is small-scale and covers ulcers; nothing exists for cosmetic use.

palifermin.text: Palifermin is a prescription keratinocyte growth factor approved for chemotherapy mouth sores, and it is occasionally mentioned in skin-renewal discussions because it stimulates epithelial cells. The evidence is for mucositis, with no cosmetic studies.

epidermal-growth-factor-egf.text: EGF is a growth-factor protein sold in skincare serums to rejuvenate skin and reduce wrinkles. The biology is well established, while evidence for the cosmetic use is one tiny serum trial with no published results.

cjc-ipa-protocol.text: CJC/IPA pairs CJC-1295 with ipamorelin and is popular on forums for muscle, leanness and recovery. The combination is untested in trials and neither part is approved; forum claims also mention water retention changing the face and eyes.

tesa-ipa-protocol.text: Tesa/IPA stacks tesamorelin with ipamorelin and is used in peptide circles for fat loss and body composition. Tesamorelin has trial data for visceral fat in a specific patient group, while the combination has no trials.

gt20029.text: GT20029 is an investigational topical AR-degrading PROTAC for male pattern hair loss and acne, discussed as a possible alternative to finasteride without systemic exposure. It has a published Phase 2 trial and is not approved.

liposomal-igf-1.text: Liposomal IGF-1 is discussed for scalp application because IGF-1 promotes follicle proliferation and the growth phase in lab work. The use is plausible on paper, and the evidence for it is preclinical.

hedgehog-pathway-agonist.text: Hedgehog pathway agonists were explored as topical hair-growth drugs because the pathway moves follicles from rest to growth. The class was discontinued, with development reportedly ended over animal toxicity.

adenosine-topical-hair.text: Topical adenosine is a cosmetic active in hair-growth products, used by people hoping to thicken thinning hair. Laboratory work reports activity on dermal papilla cells, while human evidence for this use is not established here.

procyanidin-b2.text: Procyanidin B2 is an apple polyphenol used in hair-growth tonics and discussed as a natural option for thinning hair. The evidence includes lab, mouse and small human studies, mostly using whole extracts rather than the compound alone.

garlic-gel.text: Garlic gel is a folk preparation used for patchy hair loss from alopecia areata, mostly discussed in non-prescription regrowth contexts. Evidence for that use is one terminated children's trial.

chain: Fewer wrinkles and dark spots over time
avobenzone.text: Avobenzone is the main organic UVA filter in US sunscreens and is used by people who want to slow photoageing and keep skin looking younger. UVA protection for photoageing is its studied purpose; it needs stabilisers in sunlight.
